Q1: Which branch should the fix PR target? The failure is on PR #6905's head (`orchestrator/project-6902`, `82b70181…`). Without a branch line in the issue, the pipeline targets `main`.
Choices:
A) `orchestrator/project-6902`. Treat the issue as carrying `Target branch: orchestrator/project-6902`, so the fix lands where the failing tests run and unblocks the final merge of PR #6905. (RECOMMENDED)
B) `main`. The fix reaches the project branch only after the next sync of `main` into it. If the failure comes from project-6902's own code, this cannot fix it.
C) Whichever branch the reproduced failure points to: `main` if the same test also fails there, otherwise `orchestrator/project-6902`.
Q2: What should be delivered? The log tail only shows a passing shard, so the failing test is unknown.
Choices:
A) Rerun the group-3 / shard-1 tests at the target branch head and fix only the code or test the failure points to. If nothing fails, make no code change and close the issue as transient. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Do A, and also change the shard-reporting step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (lines 1435-1437) so the `::error::` line names each failing test from that shard's log. Future triage would then not depend on the log tail. This requires a `files_touched` grant for `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
C) Make only the diagnostics change in B, with no attempt to reproduce or fix the test.
